Diagnostics:
- Job logs return 403, but check-run annotations are public. Under GitHub Actions, scripts/e2e.mjs now adds scripts/e2e-annotate.mjs, so each failed E2E test becomes an ::error annotation (file, line, assertion) and a GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY section.

- Kame (dd21add) fits the CI pattern of 3 red and 2 green runs at the same executable since 15fd171, but whether it was the unread CI assertion is unproven until a red run's annotation is read.

entries.reason: (1) /repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs/{job}/annotations returns 200 without a token while /actions/jobs/{id}/logs returns 403. Previous fix cycles treated the CI assertion as permanently unreadable, but ::error workflow commands from the E2E runner put file, line and assertion into public annotations. (2) e2e/kame.test.ts assumed an installed clock only moves with runFor; on a loaded 4-CPU Linux host the 499 ms 'not yet petted' check failed in 2 of 3 runs. (3) Building a Docker copy with 'tar --exclude=./projects' on macOS also excluded the /projects route, which produced 23 bogus 404 E2E failures. Use 'git ls-files | grep -v ^projects/ | tar -T -' instead. Also, two concurrent tasks (pm-259/t-1583 and this one) landed the same Kame repair within the hour, so git fetch before committing a repair.

entries.summary: Dropped my duplicate Kame clock pause after rebasing onto 750947b; 9ddd084 (pm-259/t-1583) landed the same pause concurrently. Only the negative control stays in this commit.
entries.reason: The contract says a failure already corrected at the delivery base must be cited, not repaired twice. 9ddd084 added page.clock.pauseAt(Date.now()+100) before the same 499/500 ms assertions in e2e/kame.test.ts. My commit keeps a negative control that resumes the clock, waits 50 real ms and shows runFor(499) already pets Kame, then re-pauses so the rest of the test runs as 9ddd084 has it. The CI diagnostics (reporter, workflow summary, server tail) are unaffected.

entries.summary: Fix the reproduced Kame E2E race: pause the installed Playwright clock before the 499/500 ms hold-threshold check, and add a negative control showing a flowing clock fools it
entries.reason: On Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.23.3, Chromium headless shell, 4 CPUs), e2e/kame.test.ts:90 failed in 2 of 3 full E2E runs at the pre-fix tree with 'Expected actual to be strictly unequal to pet' (the third run was 91/91). Playwright's types say an installed clock flows with real time until pauseAt(), so after keyboard.down('Space') plus runFor(499), real round-trip time pushes the fake clock past PET_MS=500. That is an incorrect test assumption, not an application defect: components/kame/companion.tsx's setTimeout(PET_MS) is correct. The fix pauses the clock, with a guard that real time no longer moves it, and keeps the 499-not-pet and 500-pet thresholds unchanged. The negative control resumes the clock, waits 50 real ms, then runs the same runFor(499), and Kame is petted. Kame landed in dd21add, the first commit whose E2E failures continued after the 15fd171 repair, and CI since then shows 3 red and 2 green runs at the same executable. It is the strongest reproduced candidate for the unread CI assertion, but it is not proven to be that assertion.
